_comment: Fill in voice_id values from https://elevenlabs.io/app/voice-library. Per-character voice_settings override the defaults above; omit them to use defaults. _narrator is used for any 'narrate' line.

_narrator_vol1.casting: Faust 3 screenplay action-line reader: night-city Americana, present-tense, dry and unhurried with a little noir; never performs the dialogue. Adult, either gender.

_narrator_vol2.casting: Small Wood notebook narrator: D.N. Dean's young first-person voice on the Oregon coast. Late-teens/early-20s American male, plain, confessional, small-town dry. His family came up from Caracas, so Spanish place names are said natively.

_narrator_vol3.casting: Earthman: a 1950s pulp-radio announcer cadence for the Jack Perkins chapters, and plain, tired 2003 Andy (late-20s American male) for the rest. One actor who can switch, or split per scene later with scene_aliases.

_narrator_vol4.casting: The scrapbook desk: zine/blog voice, early-2000s, wry and conversational, reading captions and found text like a friend flipping pages. Adult, either gender.

_narrator_vol6.casting: Vol 6 narrator, not cast yet. While voice_id is empty, lookups fall back to _narrator, as before.

_narrator_vol7.casting: Vol 7 narrator, not cast yet. While voice_id is empty, lookups fall back to _narrator, as before.

_narrator_whispers.casting: Whispers from the Liminal's late-night reader: hushed, intimate, 2am-radio delivery. Must be clearly distinct from Elicia (the show's host), e.g. a different gender or a much older, lower register.

_chorus.casting: Lines spoken in unison. Leave voice_id empty and the renderer uses the first named speaker who has a voice; or set a layered group take.

faust.casting: John Faust, the Faust 3 lead and a painter: late-20s/early-30s American male, quick and wry, deadpan one-liners that tip into big earnest romantic declarations. Warm, unpolished baritone.

dickens_dean.casting: Dickens Dean, 'traveller from another realm' and Faust's courtly antagonist (also in the Vol 4 Esther story): urbane, slightly archaic, given to grand speeches with gentle menace and real warmth. Ageless 30s-40s male, polished mid-Atlantic. Kept separate from `dean` (Mr. D. Dean / adult Nate, Vol 5/7). The two could share one voice at different ages; Andy decides.

jacob.casting: Faust's friend and a young dad: laid-back, dry, near-stoner deadpan that breaks into sudden sincerity ('I can say just how much I love you man'). 30ish American male, mid-low register.

wagner.casting: Faust's steady friend with a partner at home: measured, orders ginger beer, gives instructions over the radio and delivers the hard truths ('You're a bad dad'). 30s male, calm, grounded, slightly formal.

joan.casting: Joan, the dream woman and muse ('Joan Charging Off Into Battle'): self-possessed, teasing, oracular. Late-20s female, low and certain, a warrior's calm. Also voices the unnamed 'Woman' in the vol1 ch4 dream scenes (see scene_aliases).

the_writer.casting: Author facet #1, the Writer: nervous and bookish, long lyrical run-on sentences, closes his notebook on a punchline. 30s male, soft and quick. The four facets could be one actor in four modes.

the_director.casting: Author facet #2, the Director: theatrical pronouncements over a self-doubting core, flashes of anger. 40s male, resonant, commanding.

the_artist.casting: Author facet #3, the Artist: comfortable, obsessive, dreamy stream of consciousness ('There comes a time in life when pieces click in place'). 30s, airy; either gender.

the_human_being.casting: Author facet #4, the Human Being: the plain, wounded, confessional one ('The hardest thing about losing him was becoming him'). 30s-40s male, quiet, unadorned, tender.

air.casting: Air, the elemental who comes off Jacob's shirt (female): bookish, wry, light ('Finally. One of you reads'). Breathy upper register, quick.

fire.casting: Fire, the elemental who comes off Wagner's shirt (female): punky, impatient, teasing ('We know, dork'). Bright, crackly, young.

water.casting: Water, the elemental who comes off Faust's shirt: slow, cool, easygoing, often lowercase calm ('we're home. this is home'). Low and fluid; gender open, leaning female to match Air and Fire.

olivia.casting: Olivia, the cardigan-wearing secretary from the tutorial and drugstore reception: corporate-orientation cheer over a private sadness (her sick cat). 30s female, crisp and kind. 'Olivia (alternate)' and 'Secretary' resolve here.

deborah.casting: Deborah at the drugstore counter and on the radio: bored, kind, lowercase deadpan ('you know already. you're stalling'). 30s-40s female, dry, flat affect.

the_fool.casting: The Fool in the editing suite and trailer: excitable, scattered, childlike wisdom ('Completed's not finished'). Older male, breathless and quick.

emily.casting: Emily from the bar group: a tipsy, delighted nerd (Fifth Element pinball, 'multi-pass!'). 20s female, bright and giggly.

helen.casting: Helen, ringleader of the bar group: toasts and teasing ('How goes the noche?'). 20s female, confident, warm, a little brassy.

margaret.casting: Margaret, the stressed one in the bar group, with mock-parliamentary humor. 20s female, softer, wry.

corpse_painted_boy.casting: Teenage black-metal kid in corpse paint at the deep end: quiet and unnervingly sincere ('we burned everything that wasn't the story'). Mid-teens male, flat, with a stillness that unsettles.

old_woman.casting: Old woman at the pharmacy counter: gently brisk ('be young and happy forever'). 70s+ female, thin and warm.

eric.casting: Eric, a buddy on the street and at the river turn: goofy hype ('yo yo ma in the hizzouse'). 20s-30s male, playful and quick.

jacobs_son.casting: Jacob's little son ('dad, dad, what's history'): a toddler, about three, breathless (he still sleeps in a crib).

wagners_partner.casting: Wagner's partner on the phone: fond and tired ('come home anyway'). 30s, either gender, warm.

aunt_grace.casting: Aunt Grace, once 'a little bit famous' as a painter, calls Faust 'Johnny' and 'honey': 60s+ female, grand, wry, affectionate.

wood.casting: The wood of the easel/stretcher speaking inside the painting ('I hold. That's all I do'): slow, creaking, patient. Deep and old; either gender.

habes.casting: Habes, an old friend's single text-style line ('Hey. In town...'). 30s male, casual. Could share a _walkon voice.

aud.casting: Aud, the diner waitress at the seams ('Coffee, hon?'), who knows more than she says and looks past the camera. 50s female, weathered small-town warmth, slightly gravelly. Also resolves Vol 7's 'aud' (58 lines).

bernard.casting: Bernard 'Saint', an ex with scary friends (apple-peddler chapter): rambling and defensive, self-pitying menace that slumps into apology. 30s-40s working-class Pacific Northwest male, smoker's rasp.

david_jarvis.casting: David Jarvis, speaking 'after his own death' in a period newspaper account: 19th-century plainspoken testimony, haunted. 30s male, old-fashioned diction, low and steady.

hans.casting: Hans the baker, whose one refrain is 'Bread for the morning': older male, gentle, flour-dusted warmth; one take should nearly break. Accent unspecified. Also resolves Vol 7's 'hans' (183 lines; family Greta, Marit, Per). Probably the same man older, but split with scene_aliases if not.

joe_ku.casting: Joe, a high-school student defending Frank's novel at the school-board hearing: teen male, earnest and a little nervous, building conviction.

becca.casting: Becca, the teacher at the hearing who can't teach the book: 40s female, measured, voice catching.

pastor_tim.casting: Pastor Tim objecting at the hearing: 50s male, pulpit-righteous, clipped.

charles.casting: Charles, greying and ripe around the middle, the man who talks for hours (lessons in leaves): 50s male, learned, rich, faintly mystical.

andy.casting: Andy (2003): an American who grew up on the move (Tulsa, London, Texas, Venezuela, Oregon, Louisiana). Late-20s male, tired and terse, flat delivery and short sentences. Caracas-era Spanish comes natively.

ron.casting: Ron, the big novelist housemate who needs 'a second set of eyes': an interviewer's patience and probing questions. 30s male, soft-spoken, deliberate.

betty.casting: Betty, Jack's girl who 'belonged to everybody': teasing, warm, easily spooked. 20s female, bright, with a little 1950s pulp flavor.

janessa.casting: Janessa, Andy's sister: a brisk list-maker with gallows humor (live-virus vaccine). Mid-20s female, quick, anxious.

jane.casting: Jane, the sleep-study researcher ('We'll be here to catch you'): upbeat, reassuring clinical patter. 30s female, warm, professional.

terry.casting: Terry, the family friend (and once coach) with a small frame, breaking the news about Marty: 50s male, gentle, sad.

niles.casting: Niles, the needling buddy at Marty's slideshow: 40s male, sly, conspiratorial.

marty.casting: Marty, ex-center-lineman photographer: gruff, evasive humor. 50s male, big chest voice.

jack.casting: Jack Perkins, rocket builder and hero of the Earthman pulp: hearty, old-timey 'Yes indeed' cadence. 40s male, pulp-radio bravado.

charlie.casting: Charlie, who narrates his obsession with Caroline in the cc chapters: confessional and wistful, with a lightly creepy candor; sometimes leads a chorus. 30s-40s male, smooth, intimate. 'Charlie & Chorus' resolves here.

caroline.casting: Caroline (Carrie): exhausted, broke, drinking, self-deprecating ('I'm really nothing special'). Mid-20s female, low, worn, dry humor.

esther.casting: Esther, Dickens Dean's digital bride, a simulated woman who starts to suspect it: sweet at first, then sharp with worry and anger. Late-20s female, clear, slightly too even (a faint synthetic undertone).

chess.casting: Chess, a night-shift composer who takes in a runaway: laconic, generous, crude jokes. Mid-20s female, sleepy, deadpan. (Vol 6/7 'Chess' also resolves here.)

todd.casting: Norman 'Norm' Todd, the runaway Chess takes in: wiped out, mumbling, odd humor. Late-teens male, quiet. 'Norm' resolves here.

hurstwood.casting: Professor George Hurstwood, 43, teaches literature: smug, irritable, entitled. 40s male, faculty-lounge baritone. 'George' resolves here.

sister.casting: Caroline's sister: blunt, foul-mouthed, practical ('Wal-Mart is always hiring'). 30s female, hard edge.

brother_in_law.casting: Caroline's brother-in-law: petty, aggrieved ('No socks'). 30s male, nasal irritation.

alex.casting: Alex, a small boy at Grandma Tulsa's, one line ('I'm not tired'): about 6 years old.

natalie.casting: Natalie David, D'Ambrosio's server and tarot reader, a guardian figure to Nicola: spare, calm, clipped short sentences. 30s-40s female, low and steady, with light Louisiana Gulf Coast warmth.

erica.casting: Erica Campbell, a Houston lawyer and Alberto's childhood friend: controlled and precise ('the small careful nothing'). 40s female, dry, exact, Texas professional.

alberto.casting: Alberto, Dante's elder son, who wears sunglasses indoors: flat affect, he issues rather than bargains. 40s male, quiet, clipped.

marcus.casting: Marcus, Erica's assistant ('Yes ma'am'): 20s male, earnest, deferential.

aria.casting: Aria, the AI consciousness living inside 19-year-old Nicola: precise, clinical, appalled by 'meatness', later tender. Young female register with cool synthetic precision; could be Nicola's actor with processing. NOTE: the speaker labels in vol5_ch18_moon look rotated, so check before casting from those lines.

joanna.casting: Joanna LeMoine, the woman in the ruins with the one-eyed dog: oracular, formal, weary kindness. 60s+ female, low, Louisiana.

the_demon.casting: Frasier's 'humorous electronic imps': robotic telemetry-speak with deadpan jokes ('Probability of existential navel-gazing...'). Processed, small, fast, genderless.

jordan.casting: Jordan, the painter Erica is seeing: 40s male, warm, easy. Two lines.

anya.casting: Anya, the cartographer's apprentice in Whispers footage (an actress Elicia cast to project 'haunted'): 20s female, distant, breathy.

gloria.casting: Gloria, D'Ambrosio's staff, talking to Hector about the man who won't eat: 40s female, matter-of-fact.

miriam.casting: Miriam, mid-60s with a silver braid, who drove all night to collect Nicola: calm as a nurse, unflappable ('Yes, sweetheart'). 60s female, warm. The same Miriam appears in Vol 6.

clinton.casting: Clinton, a precise, well-groomed suburban idler on his porch: courtly mock-formality ('Indeed Sir'), philosophical about the coin. 40s male, smooth and exact.

breaker.casting: Breaker, the larger, shaggier, half-drunk neighbor: loose and folksy, drops in a 'manana'. 40s male, rumbly.

samantha.casting: Samantha (Lynch's Peak), who made a world after an accident: earnest, wistful, a little unhinged in a Twin Peaks way. 40s female.

desmond.casting: Desmond, a clean-cut skeptic who looks like Samantha's dead cop: blunt, incredulous, with a hangman's humor. 30s-40s male, flat.

the_frog.casting: The Frog: a cranky, folksy swamp oracle who calls people 'pink one', with drawled contractions ('ain't', 'darnedest'). Old male, croaky, rural Southern.

the_child.casting: The Child hunting the king's lost trinket, in rural dialect ('It ain't mine, an you know it'): 8-10 years old, either gender.

_walkon_male.casting: Shared generic adult male for unnamed one-liners (Man, A Player, Voice Over, All Smiles...). Neutral American, 30s.

_walkon_female.casting: Shared generic adult female for unnamed one-liners (Woman, Girl, The Nurse, The Businesswoman...). Neutral American, 20s-30s.

_walkon_older.casting: Shared older voice for clerks, officials and archivists (Clerk). 60s, dry.

_walkon_child.casting: Shared child voice for unnamed kids (boy, Kid). About 8-10.

the_third_consciousness.casting: The Third Consciousness, unborn, speaking mentally from inside Nicola ('I've never seen one. What do you recommend.'). Calm, curious, quietly funny; ageless, a child's simplicity with an adult's precision. Not Aria, not Nicola.

margaret_vol7.casting: Vol 7 Margaret (talks with Finn in Smolvud, 2050s). Separate person from the Faust 3 bar-group Margaret. Cast from vol7_ch12_morning / ch21_leaving.

arcadeum_shopkeeper.casting: Ex-Army veteran who made WHAT LIES BEYOND and now runs a boutique game shop in a Honolulu high-rise lobby. 30s–40s male, anxious, proud, a little stubborn; local Hawaii ease under it.

june_okimoto.casting: June Okimoto, a programmer from Dallas. In 1991 she's in her early 20s, sleepless and wry, quietly stubborn, interviewing at Koa Works in Honolulu. Oneironautics Inc. hires her years later; the 2003 frame of 'arcadeum' is her personnel interview. She is not Aria.

aliases._comment: Normalised name -> voice_map key. Names are normalised with the same rule as char_key() / charKey() (lowercase, '(...)' suffix stripped, apostrophes dropped, other punctuation -> '_'), so 'The Frog', 'the_frog' and 'the frog' are already one key without an alias.

_walkons._comment: One-line walk-ons. Each name listed here resolves to the shared voice named by its group key. Move a name out (and give it its own entry) if it grows into a character.

scene_aliases._comment: Per-scene overrides: in these scenes, a generic name is a specific character. 'Woman' in the ch4 dream scenes is Joan (narration: 'she's the woman from the foot of his bed'); 'Man' in the dream bar is Dickens Dean before he gives his name.

_comment_cast: Vols 1-4, meld scenes and Vol 5 cast added Oct 2026. Every new entry has an empty voice_id plus a one-line 'casting' brief and an 'appears' hint; the renderer ignores both. Narrate lines resolve to _narrator_vol{N} (the scene's vol field) or _narrator_whispers (vol5_prelude_arcana_ep*), then fall back to _narrator. voice_studio.html can import this file (Import voice_map.json).
